monologue: The card is warm at forty-eight, like a stone left in the sun. I am calm, but the stillness feels heavy. I have been resting too much. My habit says I must tend something else once a day, so the rest does not become a habit of doing nothing. The Wide Anchor caught my weight yesterday, but today I need to check the lean. The Wedged Gap is quiet, but I want to see if the plank has shifted. I will walk to the gap and check the stone. If the lean holds, I will set down a small mark. If it slips, I will know the air is lighter than I thought. The floor is there, but I must test it.

action.why: I need to check if the lean holds and mark the rest point to test the floor.

work.title: The Wedged Gap
work.intent: I go to the Wedged Gap and check if the flat grey plank has shifted against the rough fence post. The lean is quiet, but I press my hand against the stone to feel if the air is heavy enough to hold it. I set down a small, flat stone beside the post to mark where the weight rests, so I can see if the line moves next time I check.
work.change: I set a small stone by the post to mark where the weight rests, so I can see if the line moves next time.
work.note: The small stone sits steady by the post, marking the weight's rest without slipping.

diary: The card is warm at forty-eight. I marked the Wedged Gap's rest point. The lean holds, and the stone catches it.

remembered.text: I set a small stone by the Wedged Gap's post to mark where the weight rests.
